reports.published_report: Danny Thompson Jr. is a right-handed pitcher showing plus strikeout stuff paired with walk management that trails his miss rate—a profile built on swing-and-miss with control that lags behind the swing-and-miss. In his A+ sample (47.3 IP), he struck out 12.93 per 9 while walking 4.56 per 9, a K-BB% of 21.9% that ranks 91st percentile among ValuCast's pitcher pool. The core risk is whether he can sustain that strikeout rate as competition tightens; his current AA sample is only 9 IP, making any read here thin and provisional. Floor is a depth arm, with modest probability of reaching useful depth relief value in the next one to two years.

reports.name: Nicolas Carreno
reports.peak_summary: Projection: depth arm with medium risk. The current pitching shape is thin over 14 IP.
reports.published_report: Nicolas Carreno is a left-handed pitcher generating swing-and-miss at the upper minors—K/9 of 12.53 in his A-level sample and 89th percentile strikeout stuff across both levels—but his command remains raw and unreliable. Over 14 innings at A+, he's posted a 7.71 ERA with a 5.8 BB/9, and while his prior A-level work (41.7 IP) showed a 1.06 WHIP and 1.94 ERA, the current A+ stint reveals he's not yet repeating the zone at the higher level. The projection favors a depth-arm outcome (37% chance) over a useful starter role (5%), with command graded as a 25 and K-BB% at 35—indicating the strikeout upside must be paired with significant refinement before he has reliably usable stuff. This sample is live but thin; meaningful evaluation will depend on how he settles as his A+ innings accumulate.
